status_summary: H.R. 3174, the Made in America Manufacturing Finance Act, passed the House on 2025-12-01; its engrossed text defines small manufacturers (NAICS sectors 31 to 33 with all production facilities in the United States) and doubles their 7(a) guarantee limits, for example from 3.75 million to 7.5 million dollars on the standard guarantee and from 5 million to 10 million dollars on export loans, and raises a development company (504) limit to 10 million dollars. SBA's Administrator welcomed House passage, and no later Senate step was found. Separately, SBA announced on 2026-05-18 a policy, effective 2026-07-04, letting borrowers who secure a 7(a) loan first combine up to 5 million dollars of 7(a) and 5 million dollars of 504 financing; it does not create a separate larger 7(a) manufacturing category. Both fall well short of the 50 million dollar figure the chapter cites.

timeline.event: The House passed H.R. 3174, the Made in America Manufacturing Finance Act, which doubles 7(a) guarantee limits for small manufacturers and raises a 504 limit to 10 million dollars.

SBA announced a policy, which it called a new rule, letting borrowers who secure a 7(a) loan first combine 7(a) and 504 loans for up to 10 million dollars in total SBA-backed financing, effective July 4 (2026 inferred from the release date).

title: Ask Congress for a larger 7(a) loan category for manufacturing facilities and equipment
uncertainties: GovInfo lists only the House-engrossed version of H.R. 3174, with a last action date of 2025-12-01, and congress.gov could not be opened, so the absence of Senate action rests on that and on SBA and member releases. The SBA release of 2026-05-18 calls the combined-limit change a new rule but gives no Federal Register citation, SOP number or procedural notice; a Federal Register API search of SBA documents since 2026-03-01 for the term 504 found no matching rule, so the instrument is unconfirmed and it may be a policy or SOP change; the effective year 2026 is inferred from the release date. The engrossed bill text has a parenthetical on a 10 million dollar gross loan amount whose effect is unclear as drafted.
